faults.injection: finalizePost hung after the provider accepted the post; SIGKILL after 17s
faults.platform: postPending + finalizePost accepted once for post-mwctvdpc-3
faults.temporal: heartbeat timeout with details -> timeout branch -> unconfirmed, never retried
faults.knowable: yes (heartbeat details prove the mutation started; Temporal shows one accepted publish)
faults.note: The platform may have completed the finalize; the post is marked unconfirmed, not failed, and is not republished.

faults.injection: postComment hung after the provider accepted the comment; SIGKILL after ~15s
faults.platform: root published once, comment accepted once
faults.temporal: heartbeat timeout with details -> timeout branch -> unconfirmed
faults.local: comment stays QUEUE with no result; the published root is overwritten to ERROR
faults.knowable: partly (Temporal proves the root published; the comment outcome is unknown)
faults.note: markUnconfirmed targets postsList[0], so a timed-out comment also rewrites the already-published root as ERROR and leaves the comment row without a result. Recorded, not silently accepted.

faults.injection: postPending accepted then SIGKILL inside the 15s heartbeat interval
faults.platform: two accepted publishes for one post (stub-pending-87877-4, stub-pending-87973-1)
faults.temporal: heartbeat timeout without details -> classified never-started -> retried
faults.local: one PUBLISHED row pointing at the second accept; the first accept has no local record
faults.note: GENUINE HAZARD: heartbeat absence is used as "never ran". An accept that returns and then loses the worker within 15s is re-published. Pre-existing upstream behaviour; the spec forbids building a global idempotency system, so this is recorded as a residual risk.

faults.injection: checkPostStatus hangs into a 2-minute start-to-close timeout, then fails fast for the rest of the error budget
faults.platform: one accepted publish, no further mutation
faults.temporal: TimeoutFailure (START_TO_CLOSE, no details) -> bounded read-only retries -> unconfirmed
faults.knowable: yes (the publish call count stays one; only the status read is unknown)
faults.note: checkPostStatus never heartbeats and its proxy has no heartbeatTimeout, so a with-details timeout cannot occur for it. The with-details case is exercised on finalizePost in worker-death-unknown-results. Shipped schedule: 3 attempts x 2-minute start-to-close per invocation, 5 invocations with a 20-second pause, so a persistently hanging check keeps the post QUEUE for roughly 30 minutes before it is marked unconfirmed (the sweep does not restart it because the execution still exists).

faults.injection: PostsService.updatePost throws permanently after the provider completed
faults.local: post ERROR with the write-back error, no releaseId
faults.knowable: yes (Temporal shows the publish completed; the row says unconfirmed)
faults.note: Shipped retry schedule for updatePost is 3 attempts / 2-minute backoff; injected as non-retryable to bound the rehearsal. The branch reached is the same.

faults.injection: updatePost and changeState both fail after the provider completed
faults.platform: two accepted publishes for the same post
faults.temporal: first workflow completed with the row untouched; the sweep started a second run
faults.local: QUEUE row -> sweep -> second publish -> PUBLISHED
faults.knowable: no from the database (it said QUEUE); only the platform substitution shows the duplicate
faults.note: GENUINE HAZARD, pre-existing: a total write-back outage makes the local row indistinguishable from "not published", and the missing-posts sweep is a republish. Any recovery must reconcile the platform before re-running the sweep.

faults.injection: NotificationService.inAppNotification throws permanently after the publish
faults.local: post PUBLISHED with releaseId, no notification row, no e-mail
faults.knowable: yes for the post, no for the user notification
faults.note: A notification failure cannot duplicate or hide the post itself.

faults.injection: webhook URL 127.0.0.1:9 (connection refused) after the publish
faults.platform: one publish; no webhook HTTP call succeeded
faults.knowable: no for the webhook delivery (no receiver record); yes for the post
faults.note: Webhook delivery is best-effort by design; losing it is invisible locally.
No retry storm and no duplicate refresh workflow run.

faults.injection: mail provider throws on every call
faults.temporal: activity succeeded after swallowing the failure; no Temporal retry
faults.local: no delivery record, no error row
faults.note: sendEmailSync swallows the failure after three attempts, so the workflow cannot retry. Pre-existing behaviour; recorded as a delivery gap, not a duplicate hazard.

faults.injection: all workers stopped before the per-email workflow was started
faults.platform: delivery only after the worker returned
faults.temporal: activity task waited durably; exactly one execution
CONTINUED_AS_NEW with the remaining queue in the input payload
faults.knowable: yes (the successor input carries exactly the unprocessed messages)

faults.platform: one publish for the stale post
faults.note: Measured ~11 events/loop: the 24-loop gate fires at ~270 events, so the historyLength > 1000 clause cannot fire first in this release. It is a guard for a different cadence, not an exercised boundary.

faults.injection: worker registers the compiled bundle without the refreshToken activity
faults.temporal: the activity task stays scheduled; execution RUNNING (no half-run)
faults.knowable: yes (the worker names the unregistered activity; the execution is still there)
faults.note: A rollback candidate must be assembled from the annotated activity classes. A missing registration blocks instead of silently skipping the mutation, and it does not resume instantly when the annotated worker starts: the pending activity task stays leased until its start-to-close timeout (10 min, up to 3 attempts), so recovery must wait or explicitly re-drive the execution.

faults.injection: prisma db push against 127.0.0.1:1, then against the real database
faults.temporal: no execution created; nothing to resume
faults.local: rows, schema and media identical before/after; retry succeeds
faults.knowable: yes (the failed sync is non-zero and every digest still matches)
faults.note: A failed sync does not prove the schema is unchanged; this run keeps the snapshot and shows no change for this input. A partial change must be inspected from the retained error and structure, not assumed absent.

faults.injection: quiesced dump+media snapshot restored after new effects were produced
faults.platform: the refresh, the publish and the digest notification are not undone; the sweep adds a second publish
faults.temporal: same execution id/type/business id, completed, still visible
faults.local: rows and files match the backup exactly
faults.knowable: no (the restored row says QUEUE while the platform has a post)
faults.note: A simultaneous DB+media restore is consistent internally and correlates with Temporal, but it silently rolls back local knowledge of external effects. Reconcile the platform and stop re-driving sweeps before restoring under a live namespace.
